landmarks.name: To Sua Ocean Trench
landmarks.writeup: A large swimming hole formed by a collapsed lava tube, surrounded by lush gardens and cliffs.

landmarks.name: Robert Louis Stevenson Museum
landmarks.writeup: The former home of the famous Scottish author, now a museum showcasing his life and works.

landmarks.name: Lalomanu Beach
landmarks.writeup: A picturesque white sand beach known for its clear waters and coral reefs.

head_of_state: O le Ao o le Malo Tuimalealinifano Vanaletona Sualauvi II

cultural_events.name: Teuila Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual cultural festival celebrating Samoan arts, dance, and music.

cultural_events.name: Independence Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on June 1st, marking Samoa's independence from New Zealand in 1962.

food_writeup: Samoan cuisine features root vegetables like taro and breadfruit, coconut milk, fresh fish, and traditional dishes such as palusami (taro leaves with coconut cream) and oka (raw fish salad).
brief_history: Samoa was settled by Polynesians around 1000 BCE. It became a German colony in the late 19th century, then administered by New Zealand after WWI. Samoa gained independence in 1962, becoming the first Polynesian nation to do so.

important_people.name: Robert Louis Stevenson
important_people.description: Scottish author who lived in Samoa

current_conflicts: Samoa is generally peaceful with no significant current conflicts.
